findings.title: Exit code for 'recreate upgrade' changed from 4 to 3 and 4 reused for a different meaning
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 now means FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script or the Operator that already treats 4 as 'recreate required' will now read 'feature disabled' as a recreate. The Operator-side code that interprets these exit codes is not updated in this PR, so I cannot confirm it handles the new numbering. Existing docs and clients are affected even though the command is a preview.

findings.title: Custom image always bakes in rolling-updates, also for tests using the default strategy
findings.body: The build step now sets --features=rolling-updates for every use of the custom image. A build-time feature should match what the CR enables, and tests that use the default strategy with no features set may hit a mismatch. This can trigger a non-optimized start or a build-option mismatch with runtime features. The test `createInitialDeployment` sets the feature only when `updateStrategy != null`, and returns early with no feature otherwise. That means the `null` strategy case gets no feature in the CR, even though the Operator is documented to fail without the feature.

findings.title: Feature enabling is skipped for the default (null) strategy case
findings.body: For `updateStrategy == null` the method returns before enabling the `rolling-updates` feature. The docs say the feature must be enabled even for the default strategy (which mimics 26.1 behavior), and that the Operator fails otherwise. The `null` parameterized cases (testImageChange-null, testCacheMaxCount-null) therefore either run without the feature, contradicting the docs, or the Operator does not actually require it. Enable the feature before the early return so both cases are consistent.

findings.title: Feature-disabled path: exit code not tested, and features check relies on runtime Profile
findings.body: The new feature-disabled branch calls `picocli.exit(FEATURE_DISABLED)` and returns. `testFeatureNotEnabled` only asserts the error text, and only for the `metadata` subcommand. It never checks exit code 4, and `check` has no such test. The documented exit code 4 is therefore unverified.

findings.title: Doc macro appends --features after user parameters, inconsistent with prior ordering
findings.body: The macro places `--features=rolling-updates` after `${parameters}` for every use. Users who copy it are told to enable the feature, but the generated command line gives no hint that this is a preview-only requirement. It is also appended to the sample output for `check`, which could confuse readers about whether the flag belongs in a real deployment (the build vs. runtime features must match).
